confidence_note: Book not read; facts from Wikipedia, Strategyzer, a Shortform summary and publisher listings. Old text's 87-page plan, 10-minute claim and quote dropped as unsupported. No concrete company case, so the story follows the tool itself.
facts: Osterwalder's 2004 thesis on business model ontology, supervised by Yves Pigneur, led to nine blocks proposed in 2005.
Business Model Generation appeared in 2010; the publisher says 470 practitioners from 45 countries co-created it.
The nine blocks: customer segments, value propositions, channels, customer relationships, revenue streams, key resources, key activities, key partners, cost structure.
The canvas is printed large; groups fill it with sticky notes or board markers.
Right side is the market, left side what it takes to serve it, value propositions in between.
Blocks depend on each other: a new customer segment affects channels, activities and costs.
Critics call it static and light on how parts interact or on the outside world.
scene_details: a large printed sheet with nine boxes
a group standing at a wall with board markers
tension: A whole business model has to be argued about, but most descriptions bury it in long text.
opening_idea: Start with the sheet, the nine boxes and the sticky notes, before naming the author.

lessons.idea: Put the whole plan on one visible page so people can disagree about the same thing.
lessons.anchor: the nine-box sheet with sticky notes

reflect_final: Which of your projects lives only in your head, and what would writing who it serves and what it costs on one page show you?

use_cases.situation: Team argues strategy without a shared picture
use_cases.move: Draw the model on one sheet with sticky notes, customer first, then argue one box at a time.
Place it in nine boxes and note which one cannot be filled.
Ask what a different customer segment does to channels and costs, then move those notes.

pocket_idea: Nine boxes on one sheet turn a vague plan into something a team can point at and change.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A whole business model fits in nine boxes and moving one note moves the others.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Sheet, nine boxes, sticky notes, interdependence, critics call it static.
